summary_paragraph: A male patient with a history of atrial fibrillation, diastolic heart failure, severe aortic stenosis, and chronic bronchitis was admitted for worsening shortness of breath and right leg swelling. He was diagnosed with a heart failure exacerbation and cellulitis of the right lower extremity. Treatment included IV furosemide for volume overload, which improved his dyspnea, and vancomycin followed by oral antibiotics for cellulitis. His subtherapeutic digoxin and warfarin levels were corrected, though anticoagulation led to spontaneous hematomas requiring temporary hold of enoxaparin and warfarin. A right shoulder hematoma was identified and managed conservatively with pain control and elevation. Aphthous ulcers were treated with viscous lidocaine. He stabilized, completed a full antibiotic course, and was discharged to extended care with optimized heart failure and anticoagulation management, along with follow-up plans for cardiology and orthopedics.
problems: Acute on chronic diastolic heart failure
Cellulitis and abscess of leg, except foot
Coronary atherosclerosis of native coronary artery
Osteoarthrosis, localized, not specified whether primary or secondary, shoulder region
Personal history of peptic ulcer disease
Personal history of Methicillin resistant Staphylococcus aureus
